_doc: slide-builder skill settings. Read by build_deck.py at startup. Per-build CLI flags override these. Edit + save; takes effect on next invocation. The two build paths are documented in SKILL.md.
_doc_default_pattern: One of: legacy | auto | sketch | direct. 'legacy' = pptx-direct-only pipeline verbatim (the safe fallback). 'auto' = per-slide routing via _classify_all_slides. 'sketch' = force all slides through the HTML-first path. 'direct' = force all slides through the pptx-direct path (native, no HTML stage). Per-build override: build_deck.py --pattern <value>.
_doc_options_per_slide_revision: Options built when a slide is rebuilt after the user's feedback (build_deck.py --slide N, also what REVIEW.html's New design instead runs). One by default: the user has already said what to change, and one is about three times faster than three. "+3 designs" on the slide's card in REVIEW.html, or the user asking in chat, gets three for that slide. build_deck.py --options N overrides either.
_doc_options_per_slide: How many design options each slide's worker produces (1-3) on a full build and a newly inserted slide. Ships at 1 (owner's decision 2026-10-13): three cost more tokens and time (roughly 1.3-1.5x the tokens of one, unmeasured estimate). A slide gets three only when the user asks: in chat (build_deck.py --options 3 for those slides) or with "+3 designs" on that slide's card in REVIEW.html. To always get three on one computer, put {"options_per_slide": 3} in slide-builder/settings.local.json (never published; its keys win over this file; SLIDE_LAB_OPTIONS_PER_SLIDE wins over both). Read via _paths.option_letters(). NOTE: a single option is still NOT an auto-pick. REVIEW.html remains a human gate: the user picks every slide (recorded by record_picks.py), then looks at the finished picks in FINAL-CHECK.html, whose Build command carries the --final-token compile requires.
_doc_translator: How picked sketch designs become native PowerPoint. 'script' = scripts/translate_html.py (deterministic, seconds per slide; it renders its own result and hands any element it cannot draw, or that came out looking different, to the agent in fallback mode). 'agent' = the slide-builder-translator agent translates every picked option. 'script' since 2026-10-01: on 272 past options it kept 99%+ of line breaks, opened in PowerPoint, and a blind comparison of 40 slides found it closer to the design than the agent 27 to 5. Before changing the translator, the Slide Lab owner re-runs the owner's converter check (not shipped in this repository).
_doc_renderer: Which program draws slides into pictures (previews, the converter's self-check, the final check page, slide-qc, template setup). 'auto' = PowerPoint on Windows when it is installed (opened read-only without a window, never touching your open decks; it may pause for a few seconds while slides render), else LibreOffice (always on a Mac). 'powerpoint' or 'libreoffice' = start with that one. Whichever starts, if it fails a render twice the other one takes over when it is installed. SLIDE_LAB_RENDERER overrides this for one run. Read by slide-qc/scripts/render_slides.py.
_doc_enable_sketch: Master switch for the sketch (HTML-first) path. When false, default_pattern is forced to 'legacy' regardless of its value, and --pattern auto|sketch is downgraded.
_doc_html_render_canvas: Locked. Do not change without re-validating geometry across all locked specs.
_doc_ssim_thresholds: NOT ENFORCED by any script today. Intended: Critical < 0.70 halts, Major < 0.85 surfaces in REVIEW.html. In practice translator similarity scores are font-rendering noise on most slides (112 of 151 real ones scored under 0.90, and the real defects were caught by looking), so they are informational only.
_doc_translator_timeout_seconds: NOT ENFORCED by any script today: translator agents are dispatched by the chat session, which has no per-agent timeout. Kept for when translation moves to a script.
